title: Relative and Absolute Paths
summary: Understand how URLs and local paths point to resources.

sketchBlocks.title: Relative paths start from the current file
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown: A relative path tells the browser where a destination is **from the current HTML file**. ```html Tutoring schedule Campus events ``` Line by line: **First**, `schedule.html` tells the browser to look in the same folder as the current page. **Second**, `pages/events.html` tells the browser to enter the `pages` child folder before opening `events.html`. Relative paths are useful when related site files move together because the path is based on their folder relationship.

sketchBlocks.title: Absolute URLs name a complete destination
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown: An absolute URL includes the scheme and host, so the browser has the full destination. ```html Campus map ``` This line gives the browser a complete external destination: the scheme is `https`, the host is `example.org`, and `/campus-map` identifies the resource on that site. Unlike a relative path, the destination does not depend on the current HTML file's folder.

sketchBlocks.title: Use ../ to move up one folder
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown: `../` means “move to the parent folder.” If `profile.html` is inside `students/`, this link: ```html Site home ``` This line first moves from `students/` to its parent folder, then asks the browser to open `home.html` there. Read a relative path from left to right: move through the folder relationship first, then arrive at the target file.

quizDraft.title: Choose a same-folder path
quizDraft.prompt: Which href points to `about.html` in the same folder as the current page?
quizDraft.hint: A same-folder relative path can name the file directly.

help.concept: Relative paths are interpreted from the current document location.
help.hint_1: No folder change is needed for a file in the same directory.

quizDraft.title: Choose an absolute URL
quizDraft.prompt: Which destination is an absolute web URL?
quizDraft.hint: Look for a complete URL with a scheme and host.

help.concept: Absolute URLs include the full network destination.
help.hint_2: Relative paths do not need a scheme or hostname.

quizDraft.title: Recognize relative paths
quizDraft.prompt: Which values are relative paths? Choose all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: Relative paths depend on the current file location.

help.concept: Relative paths can name same-folder, child-folder, or parent-folder destinations.
help.hint_1: A full https URL is absolute.
help.hint_2: Look for values without a scheme and host.

quizDraft.title: Build a child-folder path
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange these pieces to form a relative path to `contact.html` inside the `pages` folder.
quizDraft.hint: Start with the folder, then the slash, then the file.

help.concept: A child-folder path names the folder before the file.

quizDraft.title: Complete a parent-folder path
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the prefix that moves from a child folder up to its parent before opening `index.html`.
quizDraft.hint: Use the path segment that means parent folder.

help.hint_1: The target file is outside the current folder.

quizDraft.title: Complete an external destination
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the value that makes this link point to the complete Example site profile URL.
quizDraft.hint: An external destination needs the complete absolute URL.

help.concept: Absolute web URLs include scheme and host.
help.hint_1: The destination is on example.com, not this site's folder tree.

quizDraft.title: Use a same-folder path
quizDraft.prompt: The Explorer shows `index.html` and `about.html` side by side. In `index.html`, connect `About me` to the neighboring page using a relative path.
quizDraft.hint: No folder change is needed for this destination.

help.concept: A same-folder relative path can connect sibling HTML files without a full web address.
help.hint_1: The destination file is visible beside the current file in Explorer.
help.hint_2: Use only the neighboring page's filename as the destination.

quizDraft.title: Move down into a folder
quizDraft.prompt: The robotics page is nested under the `projects` folder. In `index.html`, write the relative destination that moves into that folder and opens the page.
quizDraft.hint: Read the file tree from the current page down to the nested page.

help.concept: A child-folder relative path names the folder before the destination file.
help.hint_1: The path begins with the folder shown in Explorer.
help.hint_2: After the folder segment, name the robotics HTML file.

quizDraft.title: Move back to the parent folder
quizDraft.prompt: Open `projects/robotics.html`. Its `Back to profile` link must return to `index.html`, which is one folder above. Add the correct parent-folder relative destination, then verify both pages in Preview.

help.concept: A parent-folder relative path lets a nested page navigate to a file higher in the website tree.
help.hint_1: The current page is inside one child folder.
help.hint_2: Move up one level before naming the home page.
